content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository openhwgroup_cvfpu_pr116, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# NONCOMP clears the result bit for signaling NaNs in "not equal" compare
The NONCOMP block sets the result bit when either operand of a "not equal" comparison is a NaN:
https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu/blob/4aac6b3e87a30c8567dbe7401eba3274eea18afc/src/fpnew_noncomp.sv#L276-L279
However, it does so only for quiet NaNs, not for signaling NaNs.
While the effect of the modifier bit on comparisons is not documented, a comment in the source code indicates that its effect should be to invert the boolean result of comparisons. If either operand is a NaN, the result bit is cleared, except for a "not equal" comparison, which sets the result bit when encountering a NaN. This is in line with the way NaN values are handled in compare instructions in the RISC-V spec.
Hence, in order to treat quiet and signaling NaNs consistently and to be in line with the RISC-V spec, I suggest to modify the NONCOMP compare logic to set the result bit when either of the operands of a "not equal" compare is a signaling NaN.

64   localparam int unsigned EXP_BITS = fpnew_pkg::exp_bits(FpFormat);
65   localparam int unsigned MAN_BITS = fpnew_pkg::man_bits(FpFormat);
66   // Pipelines
67   localparam NUM_INP_REGS = (PipeConfig == fpnew_pkg::BEFORE || PipeConfig == fpnew_pkg::INSIDE)

78   // ----------------
79   // Type definition
80   // ----------------
81   typedef struct packed {
82     logic                sign;
83     logic [EXP_BITS-1:0] exponent;
84     logic [MAN_BITS-1:0] mantissa;
85   } fp_t;

87   // ---------------
88   // Input pipeline
89   // ---------------
90   // Input pipeline signals, index i holds signal after i register stages
91   logic                  [0:NUM_INP_REGS][1:0][WIDTH-1:0] inp_pipe_operands_q;
92   logic                  [0:NUM_INP_REGS][1:0]            inp_pipe_is_boxed_q;
93   fpnew_pkg::roundmode_e [0:NUM_INP_REGS]                 inp_pipe_rnd_mode_q;
94   fpnew_pkg::operation_e [0:NUM_INP_REGS]                 inp_pipe_op_q;
95   logic                  [0:NUM_INP_REGS]                 inp_pipe_op_mod_q;
96   TagType                [0:NUM_INP_REGS]                 inp_pipe_tag_q;
97   logic                  [0:NUM_INP_REGS]                 inp_pipe_mask_q;
98   AuxType                [0:NUM_INP_REGS]                 inp_pipe_aux_q;
99   logic                  [0:NUM_INP_REGS]                 inp_pipe_valid_q;
100   // Ready signal is combinatorial for all stages
101   logic [0:NUM_INP_REGS] inp_pipe_ready;
102 
103   // Input stage: First element of pipeline is taken from inputs
104   assign inp_pipe_operands_q[0] = operands_i;
105   assign inp_pipe_is_boxed_q[0] = is_boxed_i;
106   assign inp_pipe_rnd_mode_q[0] = rnd_mode_i;
107   assign inp_pipe_op_q[0]       = op_i;
108   assign inp_pipe_op_mod_q[0]   = op_mod_i;
109   assign inp_pipe_tag_q[0]      = tag_i;
110   assign inp_pipe_mask_q[0]     = mask_i;
111   assign inp_pipe_aux_q[0]      = aux_i;
112   assign inp_pipe_valid_q[0]    = in_valid_i;
113   // Input stage: Propagate pipeline ready signal to updtream circuitry
114   assign in_ready_o = inp_pipe_ready[0];
115   // Generate the register stages
116   for (genvar i = 0; i < NUM_INP_REGS; i++) begin : gen_input_pipeline
117     // Internal register enable for this stage
118     logic reg_ena;
119     // Determine the ready signal of the current stage - advance the pipeline:
120     // 1. if the next stage is ready for our data
121     // 2. if the next stage only holds a bubble (not valid) -> we can pop it
122     assign inp_pipe_ready[i] = inp_pipe_ready[i+1] | ~inp_pipe_valid_q[i+1];
123     // Valid: enabled by ready signal, synchronous clear with the flush signal
124     `FFLARNC(inp_pipe_valid_q[i+1], inp_pipe_valid_q[i], inp_pipe_ready[i], flush_i, 1'b0, clk_i, rst_ni)
125     // Enable register if pipleine ready and a valid data item is present
126     assign reg_ena = (inp_pipe_ready[i] & inp_pipe_valid_q[i]) | reg_ena_i[i];

128     `FFL(inp_pipe_operands_q[i+1], inp_pipe_operands_q[i], reg_ena, '0)
129     `FFL(inp_pipe_is_boxed_q[i+1], inp_pipe_is_boxed_q[i], reg_ena, '0)

131     `FFL(inp_pipe_op_q[i+1],       inp_pipe_op_q[i],       reg_ena, fpnew_pkg::FMADD)
132     `FFL(inp_pipe_op_mod_q[i+1],   inp_pipe_op_mod_q[i],   reg_ena, '0)
133     `FFL(inp_pipe_tag_q[i+1],      inp_pipe_tag_q[i],      reg_ena, TagType'('0))
134     `FFL(inp_pipe_mask_q[i+1],     inp_pipe_mask_q[i],     reg_ena, '0)
135     `FFL(inp_pipe_aux_q[i+1],      inp_pipe_aux_q[i],      reg_ena, AuxType'('0))
136   end

138   // ---------------------
139   // Input classification
140   // ---------------------
141   fpnew_pkg::fp_info_t [1:0] info_q;
142 
143   // Classify input
144   fpnew_classifier #(
145     .FpFormat    ( FpFormat ),
146     .NumOperands ( 2        )
147     ) i_class_a (
148     .operands_i ( inp_pipe_operands_q[NUM_INP_REGS] ),

153   fp_t                 operand_a, operand_b;
154   fpnew_pkg::fp_info_t info_a,    info_b;
155 
156   // Packing-order-agnostic assignments
157   assign operand_a = inp_pipe_operands_q[NUM_INP_REGS][0];
158   assign operand_b = inp_pipe_operands_q[NUM_INP_REGS][1];
159   assign info_a    = info_q[0];
160   assign info_b    = info_q[1];
161 
162   logic any_operand_inf;
163   logic any_operand_nan;
164   logic signalling_nan;
165 
166   // Reduction for special case handling
167   assign any_operand_inf = (| {info_a.is_inf,        info_b.is_inf});
168   assign any_operand_nan = (| {info_a.is_nan,        info_b.is_nan});
169   assign signalling_nan  = (| {info_a.is_signalling, info_b.is_signalling});
170 
171   logic operands_equal, operand_a_smaller;
172 
173   // Equality checks for zeroes too
174   assign operands_equal    = (operand_a == operand_b) || (info_a.is_zero && info_b.is_zero);
175   // Invert result if non-zero signs involved (unsigned comparison)
176   assign operand_a_smaller = (operand_a < operand_b) ^ (operand_a.sign || operand_b.sign);

178   // ---------------
179   // Sign Injection
180   // ---------------
181   fp_t                sgnj_result;
182   fpnew_pkg::status_t sgnj_status;
183   logic               sgnj_extension_bit;
184 
185   // Sign Injection - operation is encoded in rnd_mode_q:
186   // RNE = SGNJ, RTZ = SGNJN, RDN = SGNJX, RUP = Passthrough (no NaN-box check)
187   always_comb begin : sign_injections
188     logic sign_a, sign_b; // internal signs
189     // Default assignment
190     sgnj_result = operand_a; // result based on operand a
191 
192     // NaN-boxing check will treat invalid inputs as canonical NaNs
193     if (!info_a.is_boxed) sgnj_result = '{sign: 1'b0, exponent: '1, mantissa: 2**(MAN_BITS-1)};
194 
195     // Internal signs are treated as positive in case of non-NaN-boxed values
196     sign_a = operand_a.sign & info_a.is_boxed;
197     sign_b = operand_b.sign & info_b.is_boxed;
198 
199     // Do the sign injection based on rm field
200     unique case (inp_pipe_rnd_mode_q[NUM_INP_REGS])
201       fpnew_pkg::RNE: sgnj_result.sign = sign_b;          // SGNJ
202       fpnew_pkg::RTZ: sgnj_result.sign = ~sign_b;         // SGNJN
203       fpnew_pkg::RDN: sgnj_result.sign = sign_a ^ sign_b; // SGNJX
204       fpnew_pkg::RUP: sgnj_result      = operand_a;       // passthrough
205       default: sgnj_result = '{default: fpnew_pkg::DONT_CARE}; // don't care
206     endcase
207   end
208 
209   assign sgnj_status = '0;        // sign injections never raise exceptions
210 
211   // op_mod_q enables integer sign-extension of result (for storing to integer regfile)
212   assign sgnj_extension_bit = inp_pipe_op_mod_q[NUM_INP_REGS] ? sgnj_result.sign : 1'b1;
213 
214   // ------------------
215   // Minimum / Maximum
216   // ------------------
217   fp_t                minmax_result;
218   fpnew_pkg::status_t minmax_status;
219   logic               minmax_extension_bit;
220 
221   // Minimum/Maximum - operation is encoded in rnd_mode_q:
222   // RNE = MIN, RTZ = MAX
223   always_comb begin : min_max
224     // Default assignment
225     minmax_status = '0;
226 
227     // Min/Max use quiet comparisons - only sNaN are invalid
228     minmax_status.NV = signalling_nan;
229 
230     // Both NaN inputs cause a NaN output
231     if (info_a.is_nan && info_b.is_nan)
232       minmax_result = '{sign: 1'b0, exponent: '1, mantissa: 2**(MAN_BITS-1)}; // canonical qNaN
233     // If one operand is NaN, the non-NaN operand is returned
234     else if (info_a.is_nan) minmax_result = operand_b;
235     else if (info_b.is_nan) minmax_result = operand_a;
236     // Otherwise decide according to the operation
237     else begin
238       unique case (inp_pipe_rnd_mode_q[NUM_INP_REGS])
239         fpnew_pkg::RNE: minmax_result = operand_a_smaller ? operand_a : operand_b; // MIN
240         fpnew_pkg::RTZ: minmax_result = operand_a_smaller ? operand_b : operand_a; // MAX
241         default: minmax_result = '{default: fpnew_pkg::DONT_CARE}; // don't care
242       endcase
243     end
244   end
245 
246   assign minmax_extension_bit = 1'b1; // NaN-box as result is always a float value
247 
248   // ------------
249   // Comparisons
250   // ------------
251   fp_t                cmp_result;
252   fpnew_pkg::status_t cmp_status;
253   logic               cmp_extension_bit;
254 
255   // Comparisons - operation is encoded in rnd_mode_q:
256   // RNE = LE, RTZ = LT, RDN = EQ
257   // op_mod_q inverts boolean outputs
258   always_comb begin : comparisons
259     // Default assignment
260     cmp_result = '0; // false
261     cmp_status = '0; // no flags
262 
263     // Signalling NaNs always compare as false and are illegal
264     if (signalling_nan) cmp_status.NV = 1'b1; // invalid operation
265     // Otherwise do comparisons
266     else begin
267       unique case (inp_pipe_rnd_mode_q[NUM_INP_REGS])
268         fpnew_pkg::RNE: begin // Less than or equal
269           if (any_operand_nan) cmp_status.NV = 1'b1; // Signalling comparison: NaNs are invalid
270           else cmp_result = (operand_a_smaller | operands_equal) ^ inp_pipe_op_mod_q[NUM_INP_REGS];
271         end
272         fpnew_pkg::RTZ: begin // Less than
273           if (any_operand_nan) cmp_status.NV = 1'b1; // Signalling comparison: NaNs are invalid
274           else cmp_result = (operand_a_smaller & ~operands_equal) ^ inp_pipe_op_mod_q[NUM_INP_REGS];
275         end
276         fpnew_pkg::RDN: begin // Equal
277           if (any_operand_nan) cmp_result = inp_pipe_op_mod_q[NUM_INP_REGS]; // NaN always not equal
278           else cmp_result = operands_equal ^ inp_pipe_op_mod_q[NUM_INP_REGS];
279         end
280         default: cmp_result = '{default: fpnew_pkg::DONT_CARE}; // don't care
281       endcase
282     end
283   end
284 
285   assign cmp_extension_bit = 1'b0; // Comparisons always produce booleans in integer registers

288   // Classification
289   // ---------------
290   fpnew_pkg::status_t    class_status;
291   logic                  class_extension_bit;
292   fpnew_pkg::classmask_e class_mask_d; // the result is actually here
293 
294   // Classification - always return the classification mask on the dedicated port
295   always_comb begin : classify
296     if (info_a.is_normal) begin
297       class_mask_d = operand_a.sign       ? fpnew_pkg::NEGNORM    : fpnew_pkg::POSNORM;
298     end else if (info_a.is_subnormal) begin
299       class_mask_d = operand_a.sign       ? fpnew_pkg::NEGSUBNORM : fpnew_pkg::POSSUBNORM;
300     end else if (info_a.is_zero) begin
301       class_mask_d = operand_a.sign       ? fpnew_pkg::NEGZERO    : fpnew_pkg::POSZERO;
302     end else if (info_a.is_inf) begin
303       class_mask_d = operand_a.sign       ? fpnew_pkg::NEGINF     : fpnew_pkg::POSINF;
304     end else if (info_a.is_nan) begin
305       class_mask_d = info_a.is_signalling ? fpnew_pkg::SNAN       : fpnew_pkg::QNAN;
306     end else begin
307       class_mask_d = fpnew_pkg::QNAN; // default value
308     end
309   end
310 
311   assign class_status        = '0;   // classification does not set flags
312   assign class_extension_bit = 1'b0; // classification always produces results in integer registers
313

315   // Result selection
316   // -----------------
317   fp_t                   result_d;
318   fpnew_pkg::status_t    status_d;
319   logic                  extension_bit_d;
320   logic                  is_class_d;
321

339       end

342         status_d        = class_status;
343         extension_bit_d = class_extension_bit;
344       end
345       default: begin
346         result_d        = '{default: fpnew_pkg::DONT_CARE}; // dont care
347         status_d        = '{default: fpnew_pkg::DONT_CARE}; // dont care
348         extension_bit_d = fpnew_pkg::DONT_CARE;             // dont care
349       end
350     endcase
351   end
352 
353   assign is_class_d = (inp_pipe_op_q[NUM_INP_REGS] == fpnew_pkg::CLASSIFY);

358   // Output pipeline signals, index i holds signal after i register stages

372   assign out_pipe_result_q[0]        = result_d;
373   assign out_pipe_status_q[0]        = status_d;
374   assign out_pipe_extension_bit_q[0] = extension_bit_d;
375   assign out_pipe_class_mask_q[0]    = class_mask_d;
376   assign out_pipe_is_class_q[0]      = is_class_d;
377   assign out_pipe_tag_q[0]           = inp_pipe_tag_q[NUM_INP_REGS];
378   assign out_pipe_mask_q[0]          = inp_pipe_mask_q[NUM_INP_REGS];

382   assign inp_pipe_ready[NUM_INP_REGS] = out_pipe_ready[0];
383   // Generate the register stages
384   for (genvar i = 0; i < NUM_OUT_REGS; i++) begin : gen_output_pipeline

414   assign mask_o          = out_pipe_mask_q[NUM_OUT_REGS];

<analysis>
The issue arises in the “comparisons” always_comb block around lines 258–283 of src/fpnew_noncomp.sv.  Currently, a signaling NaN (signalling_nan==1) short-circuits the comparison: cmp_status.NV is set, but cmp_result is left at its default ‘0’.  For the RDN (= Equal) case with op_mod=1 (“not equal”) the spec requires the result bit to be “1” even on a signaling NaN (while still raising NV).  

To fix this, we must:
1. Refactor the outer `if (signalling_nan)` so that NV is flagged but the RDN case can still drive cmp_result.
2. Update the RDN case so that any NaN (quiet or signaling) yields `cmp_result = op_mod`.
3. Ensure that “signalling_nan” and “any_operand_nan” wiring are clear, and potentially add a separate quiet-NaN wire if needed for future clarity.  

Thus we need to touch at least these locations:
- The assignment of `signalling_nan` and `any_operand_nan` (lines 168–170).
- The outer signaling-NaN check in the comparisons block (lines 263–266).
- The RDN (= Equal) case inside comparisons (lines 276–279).
</analysis>
